steps.label: Echo Check and ARQ
steps.content:
2.2 Methods of Error Detection

Echo Check and ARQ

Year 10

  • Today: two ways for the receiver to reply to the sender: the echo check and automatic repeat query (ARQ).
  • You already know: the parity check and the checksum. The receiver checks the data.
Think → Pair → ShareThe receiver finds an error. How does the SENDER find out that it must send the data again?Show the answer

It cannot see the data that arrived. Something must go back from the receiver to the sender. Today we learn two ways.

steps.label: The Echo Check
steps.content:
The Echo Check

Think → Pair → SharePredict: the sender sends 01011010. The copy that comes back is 01001010. What does the sender notice? What should it do?Show the worked answer

The fourth bit is different: 1 went, 0 came back. The copy does not match, so there is an error.

The sender sends the data again. This is an echo check.

  • The sender sends the data.
  • The receiver sends a copy of the data it got back to the sender.
  • The sender compares the copy with the data it sent.
  • The same: no error. Different: an error, so the sender sends the data again.

steps.label: Check: The Echo Check
steps.content:
Check: The Echo Check

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must the receiver send back what it GOT, not what it expected?Show the answer

The sender needs to see what really arrived, so it can compare.

Answer in one or two words.

Total: 3 marks

steps.label: Exam Question: How the Echo Check Works
steps.content:
Exam Question: How the Echo Check Works

Think → Pair → ShareThis has 3 marks. What are the three steps?Show the answer

The copy is sent back; the sender compares; different means an error.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2024, Question 2(f). An employee emails a report to their employer. The email data is checked for errors after it has been transmitted, using an echo check and a checksum.

items.prompt: (i) Explain how the echo check is used to check for errors in the email data. [3]
items.modelAnswer: A copy of the data is sent back to the employee's device (the sender); the sender compares the data sent with the data received back; if the original and the copy do not match, an error has occurred.

steps.label: Compare: There or Back?
steps.content:
Compare: There or Back?

Think → Pair → ShareThe same byte was sent three times. Where did each error happen? The sender only sees the top row and the bottom row. Can it tell A and B apart?Show the answer

A: a bit changed on the way there. The receiver sent back what it got.

B: the data arrived correctly. A bit changed on the way back.

C: no error.

In A and B the sender sees the same thing: a copy that does not match. It cannot tell which way the error happened, so it sends the data again both times. The data also travels twice, so an echo check takes longer.

ABC
Sent by the sender101101001011010010110100
Arrived at the receiver100101001011010010110100
Copy back at the sender100101001011000010110100
  • The sender only sees the data it sent and the copy back.
  • The data goes there and back: it travels twice.

steps.label: Exam Question: The Tractor and the Echo Check
steps.content:
Exam Question: The Tractor and the Echo Check

Think → Pair → ShareWhich one is the sender here, and which one is the receiver?Show the answer

The tractor sends the data, so the tractor compares. The computer receives it, so it sends the copy back.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2024, Question 6(e). At the end of each day a self-driving tractor transmits the data it has collected to the farmer's computer in their house. The transmission uses an echo check.

items.prompt: (i) Describe the role of the self-driving tractor and the farmer's computer in the echo check. [3]
items.modelAnswer: Any three: the farmer's computer transmits the same data back to the tractor; the tractor compares both sets of data; if they are identical there is no error; if they are different, the tractor resends the data (or reports an error).

steps.label: Automatic Repeat Query (ARQ)
steps.content:
Automatic Repeat Query (ARQ)

Think → Pair → SharePredict: the sender sends packet 2 and starts a timer. The timer runs out. Nothing came back. What should the sender do?Show the worked answer

Send packet 2 again. Nothing came back, so the sender cannot be sure packet 2 arrived correctly.

The timer running out is called a timeout.

  • The sender sends the data and starts a timer.
  • The receiver checks the data, for example with a parity check.
  • No error: the receiver sends a positive acknowledgement back. It means "it arrived correctly".
  • The acknowledgement arrives in time: the sender sends the next data.
  • Nothing arrives before the timer runs out (a timeout): the sender sends the data again.

Same: the sender sends packet 2 again.

Different: with positive acknowledgement the receiver sends nothing, so the sender waits for the timeout. With negative acknowledgement the receiver sends a negative acknowledgement, so the sender knows straight away.

steps.label: Check: What a Timeout Means
steps.content:
Check: What a Timeout Means

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can the sender not know WHY nothing came back?Show the answer

It cannot see the packet or the receiver. It only knows that nothing arrived in time.

ARQ with positive acknowledgement. The sender sent packet 6 and started the timer.

items.prompt: A timeout happens. What does the sender know?
items.explain: A timeout only means the timer ran out before an acknowledgement arrived. Packet 6 may have been lost or had an error, or the acknowledgement may have been lost. So the sender sends packet 6 again.

steps.label: Activity 2: Be the Sender, Be the Receiver
steps.content:
Activity 2: Be the Sender, Be the Receiver

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does the sender keep a copy of each packet until it is acknowledged?Show the answer

It may need to send it again after a timeout or a negative acknowledgement.

Be the receiver: check the byte and decide what to send back. Be the sender: decide which packet to send next. New bytes and packets every time.

steps.label: Exam Question: ARQ with Positive Acknowledgement
steps.content:
Exam Question: ARQ with Positive Acknowledgement

Think → Pair → ShareThis has 5 marks. Use the timeline: what happens at each step?Show the answer

Timer starts; receiver checks; acknowledgement sent; next packet sent; no acknowledgement means timeout, so the packet is sent again.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, November 2023, Question 5(c). An automatic repeat query (ARQ) can be used to make sure that data is received free of errors. It can use a positive or negative acknowledgement method to do this.

items.prompt: Explain how an ARQ operates using a positive acknowledgement method. [5]
items.modelAnswer: Any five: a timer is started when the sending device transmits a data packet to the receiver; the receiving device checks the data packet for errors; once the receiving device knows the packet is error free it sends an acknowledgement back to the sending device; and the next packet is sent; if the sending device does not receive an acknowledgement before the timer ends, a timeout occurs; the data packet is resent; until an acknowledgement is received, or until a maximum number of attempts is reached.

steps.label: Exam Question: Checksum and ARQ Together
steps.content:
Exam Question: Checksum and ARQ Together

Think → Pair → ShareWhat does each one do? Which one finds the error, and which one gets the data sent again?Show the answer

The checksum finds the error. ARQ makes sure the data arrives, and asks for it again if there is an error.

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2022, Question 7(c). Umar's data is sent to a file server. Checksum and ARQ are both used when transmitting the data from a computer to the file server.

items.prompt: Explain why checksum and ARQ are both used. [3]
items.modelAnswer: Any three (at most two about ARQ): the checksum is used to detect errors during transmission, using a calculated value; ARQ checks that the data is received; it uses acknowledgement and timeout; it requests that the data is sent again if the checksum detects an error or the data is not received.
